quest.title: As by a God's Side
quest.description: As your plan progresses, more and more preparations have been done for the important day. However, this does not mean the process is as smooth as can be...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x975, Primogem x30, Mora x38600, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.title: Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises

talks.objective: Go to Caravan Ribat to meet up with Dehya

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya~! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It's about time! Didn't you say our part of the plan is the most important of all? Tsk, and here you come rolling in late.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: In the time it took you to get here, I already did five laps around the place, downed seven drinks, and even did some clothes shopping.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, sorry... We didn't mean to keep you waiting...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Heh, I just wanted to fix your attitude and rub it in a little. After all, you took your sweet time getting here, and we've got important stuff to take care of.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry, the situation was a bit tricky.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Haha, I just like seeing that serious look on your face. Alright, I'll stop.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: All joking aside, I'm glad you're here. Let's get moving and take care of this as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, but where should we start?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Our responsibility is to get a status update on the Fatui Harbinger known as The Doctor. We need to make sure he won't get in our way when we rescue Lesser Lord Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Dealing with an institution that controls all of Sumeru is already hard enough... If The Doctor were to crash the party, it would be next to impossible for us to achieve our goals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we sure don't want him showing up... Ugh, he really gives Paimon the creeps!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Right, hearing his name just reminds me of those stuffy old geezers in the Akademiya. I'd rather not have to deal with someone like that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what should we do?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: According to the plan, we should first go to Pardis Dhyai, and ask for Forest Watcher Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If Alhaitham and Cyno's sources are solid, then we can be sure that Tighnari still has the Akademiya's trust.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So, we'll find Tighnari, and convince him to get us the latest intel on The Doctor. Then, depending on what we learn, we'll make any necessary adjustments to our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The sages have placed spies everywhere on the other side of the Wall. I'll follow you as a bodyguard.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I didn't expect you to become my bodyguard.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haha, you should be honored. I don't offer my services to just anyone, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon thought mercenaries would do anything for Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's certainly true, but when multiple employers are vying for your services, you should always go with the best offer. Hmm, let's see. If I were to charge you a bill... I guess I can apply a discount.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—How much Mora do you want? Paimon's not sure we can afford it...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm, how much do I want...? Hey, how about paying me with a smile, whaddya say?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I haven't seen you smiling much recently. If you ask me, someone like you must look lovely when they smile.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Come on, give me a smile so that I can be less worried.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Thank you, Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Looking good! I hope this pretty smile will become our lucky charm.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: There are many kinds of smiles, but only a truly joyous one can bring blessings to others. Let's consider this smile a down payment for our future victory.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Let's go! It's time to pay a visit to Pardis Dhyai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tighnari!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and you are...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Long time no see!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is our friend, Dehya. She's an Eremite mercenary!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: A mercenary... Hmm, you must have some big news for me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tighnari, we want to ask you about something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's something really important! Please help us out.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, then follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This place is better. We won't be disturbed by any passerby.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Okay, what is this important thing you want to ask me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you ever met The Doctor?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I want to know where he is.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Doctor, hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's that strange-looking Fatui Harbinger with a mask! Paimon thinks he has blue hair.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, I know him.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Actually, he left Pardis Dhyai just a little while ago.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: He left already?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yeah, he came looking for me.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Can I ask what it was about?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sorry to ask you like this after having just met, but your answer is very important to us.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: For now, all we can share with you is that... your friend Cyno is working with us.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Cyno, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...I see, so that's why he hasn't been at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Okay, I will answer your questions and will assist you any way I can. You don't have to tell me everything that's happened.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hahaha, Cyno's name really does work wonders. You're not even a little worried that we might've made it all up?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #Despite having just met you, I can sense that you're the serious type. Between you, {NICKNAME}, and Cyno, none of you strike me as the type that would conspire to deceive me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You don't need to tell me anything you don't want to. I'll also get straight to the point.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Harbinger you mentioned came to me because he wanted to take the scholar Haypasia away with him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haypasia!? Why would he want her?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is he after?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: And what do you mean by "take away"? Is he planning to leave Sumeru?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, he told me his return to Snezhnaya is imminent.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hmph... so you mean, you're leaving this place soon?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Indeed. Otherwise, we could have perhaps talked a little more.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I was just about to set out when I remembered something important. To that end, I made a final trip to Pardis Dhyai.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Let me ask... have you been taking care of a scholar by the name of Haypasia?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Your sources are accurate, no doubt because you have recruited many informants, but you are right, Haypasia has indeed been receiving treatment from me.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Forgive me for asking, but how's the treatment coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Given the way you're asking, I assume you have something to say?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Since you asked, I'll be frank: I would like to take Haypasia to Snezhnaya.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's incredibly difficult to transfer a patient. As a scholar yourself, shouldn't you at least be aware of this?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Oh? I can't believe your utter lack of faith in me, to the point of even questioning my general level of knowledge. How unbefitting.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, you're the only one who's ever made such a request.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I have my ways of keeping her safe during the journey. In addition, I can also promise that under my care, Haypasia will receive the most advanced and effective treatment.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I will personally supervise her treatment and see to her recovery. Would that be agreeable to you?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Haypasia was born in Sumeru, and remains a scholar of the Akademiya. Her situation has not become dire enough to necessitate her transfer to another nation.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Transporting her to Snezhnaya is risky, and the potential benefits are unknown. As the person currently responsible for her treatment, I cannot possibly sign off on this transfer.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Your suggestion is rude and reckless. I'll pass.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I don't know much about The Doctor. But after talking with him, I realized that just like many other scholars, he possesses an aura of arrogance that I've come to detest.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's not so much that he's looking down on others, but more that he's confident in himself and his abilities to a point of near insanity.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I would never refer a patient to someone like him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you think he'll just give up on her?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I prepared myself for a protracted battle of wits, and was really surprised to see him just give up on the topic. Still, his reaction really concerned me...

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: ...Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: I see, I see. Of course, your opinion makes perfect sense.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Hehe... You're still young, but already quite stubborn. I must say, you are not like what I had expected...

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Under normal circumstances, I wouldn't just let you off the hook like this, but unfortunately, I'm in a hurry today — what with Her Most Noble Majesty, the Tsaritsa, calling for our return.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: Luckily, there is still some time left for me to take care of everything before I leave.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: It's just as the Akademiya said — you're a responsible and gifted scholar. Sadly, even with all of that, you're still lacking a bit of shrewdness.

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: And that's also why people like you can never realize that sooner or later, everyone must pay the price for what they've learned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon can't help but feel like he's hinting at something unpleasant...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: He asked a question, yet didn't care for my answer. Perhaps I'm nothing but a talking rock in his eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: He never came off as malicious, but an utter lack of compassion permeated throughout our conversation. From his tone, I can sense that he's always looked down on others.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't believe he is actually leaving Sumeru...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I can barely believe it myself. But if that's true, the situation will be in our favor.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I don't think I missed any details. Frankly speaking, I don't want you to do anything too risky. Now that you know a little more, it should be easier for you to stay safe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you for sharing the information with us, Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sorry we can't tell you everything. We appreciate that you helped us anyway. I won't forget your kindness.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's okay, I have an obligation to do so. To be perfectly honest... all of this may have started because of me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Recently, my master wrote several letters to me, asking me to return to the Akademiya and assist him with his research.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hasn't he already asked you several times before?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, but there's something off about this most recent batch of letters. The handwriting and tone are both familiar, but some details have been omitted...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: My master will occasionally leave a few dots on the back of the letter. One dot means that he wrote the letter on a sunny day, and three dots stand for a rainy day.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This has been a habit of his for many years. But I didn't find any dots in his recent letters. I believe... something may have happened to him.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I get it. Since you are always at Gandharva Ville, you would like me — someone already working at the Akademiya — to investigate this matter, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'd like to ask you to do that for me, if you can keep yourself safe. Please withdraw immediately at the first hint of danger.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I can do that, but I have a feeling it won't be that simple.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Akademiya has been working on a big project. I'm not quite sure what it is, but your master might be involved with it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If the higher-ups really are hiding something, then it will be difficult to remove myself from the situation once the investigation starts.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If the situation becomes critical, I'll leave the Akademiya. If you don't see me there for an extended period, that's your cue.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, we've got a plan. I'll stay at Gandharva Ville to support you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If that scenario comes to pass, you must be extra vigilant, and be wary of any messages or direct requests from the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I must say, I didn't expect a warning like this from the General Mahamatra.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Being loyal to the Akademiya doesn't mean blindly doing whatever the sages say. I know what I'm doing.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: On that note, aren't you also being quite distrustful of your alma mater?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Akademiya, yes. But my master is a man of integrity. Even when I was a student, I was worried that he'd get in trouble for sticking to his beliefs.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I suppose he's lucky to have lasted so long... but in the end, it still caught up to him.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I see... so you noticed something was up with the Akademiya from the very beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This may well be how Cyno became involved in all of this. In which case, I must keep my promise, and help you however I can.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Also, if you run into Cyno again, please help me pass on a message to him: "Trust your own senses and experiences."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I think this may be something he needs to hear right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we'll find a chance to tell him!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Right, now let's go hunt down this Harbinger...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh, by the way, which way did The Doctor go when he left Pardis Dhyai?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That way.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Gotcha, thanks so much. We'll be on our way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you later!

talks.objective: Talk to Dehya after leaving Pardis Dhyai

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: According to Tighnari, The Doctor is leaving Sumeru soon. I want to check if The Doctor was actually telling the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: He also said that he will "take care of everything" before he leaves. What did he mean by that? We need to be extra careful when dealing with a person like him.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Just to be safe, let's chase him and see what we find.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we have no idea where he went. How can we start chasing him?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We'll do it the mercenary way. I'll find leads as we go, all you have to do is just follow me.

talks.objective: Track The Doctor down together with Dehya

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You can just focus on your plan. Leave Haypasia to me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: My wound isn't going to get in the way... Argh! Okay... Guess I'll sit still for a little while longer.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We can stop here. I think I know where The Doctor went.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: To the south of here is Port Ormos, which seems to be where they're headed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Port Ormos... they're going to leave by boat?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's right. Let's go to the port and have a look for ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, Fatui soldiers!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks to Dehya's tracking skills, seems we've found the right place!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Shh, don't draw their attention.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The port is crawling with Fatui soldiers...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's keep going and see what we can find!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: "Sooner or later, everyone must pay the price for what they've learned"... Hmph, what an arrogant statement.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, don't mind me, I was just thinking about his words. Be sure to take extra care of yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: This place will do. We can hide here while we keep an eye on the boat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So The Doctor didn't lie about leaving Sumeru... But, could it really be that simple?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are we sure he's not planning something...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh oh!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He... he saw us...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Huh, is he waving at us?

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: It's time to say goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wait, is he the only person on the boat?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean there's nobody with him?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...And where are all the soldiers we saw in the port just now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They were all here just a few minutes ago, but now, they've vanished...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So this was a trap...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But there's nobody around us.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wait, don't tell me that...

dialogues.speaker: The Doctor
dialogues.text: "Luckily, there is still time left for me to take care of everything before I leave."

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh no...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh-oh!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: They might be after Haypasia. Let's get back to Pardis Dhyai!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I'm afraid that she's seen something that she wasn't supposed to see. If I were the Fatui, I would also try to take her away. And if I couldn't...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no! Are you saying they're going to kill her!?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Let's go!

choices.text: Haypasia once connected her consciousness to The Balladeer...

talks.objective: Return to Pardis Dhyai as quickly as possible

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Pardis Dhyai is not a place you Fatui can just show up and do as you please.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: I believe we've already made ourselves quite clear. Our superior gave us permission to search for and collect medicinal herbs in Pardis Dhyai for research purposes.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But you've been in Sumeru for some time already. I find it coincidental that you chose to only come here today.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: Even the Grand Sage himself may not have the right to question our research, much less an ordinary scholar like yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: I've done my duty to inform you. Don't make things difficult for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It would seem that my words have fallen on deaf ears.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You can keep trying to deny it, but coming to Pardis Dhyai now? I'm pretty sure you're not just looking for herbs.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: With all due respect, your baseless speculations will only lead to unnecessary trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, you only have your Harbinger to blame. He knows nothing about keeping a low profile.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I may be staying at Pardis Dhyai as a scholar, but that doesn't mean I'm no longer a Forest Watcher.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It is still my duty to protect the peace and safety of the scholars who have contributed so much to Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: Then it seems our conversation has hit an impasse.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: No one will lay a hand on you, Haypasia... Not on my watch!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #We're not getting anywhere... {NICKNAME}, Paimon, please go to Haypasia. We need to make sure they don't try to sneak around and attack from behind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haypasia's still here. Doesn't look like anyone's broken in...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She appears unharmed, but why is she so still?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Phew, she's just sleeping.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, how is she?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Everything's fine. She's sound asleep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that's good...
So, you think this is over.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That voice...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Balladeer!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What! The Balladeer is here!?
Haha, I've missed that look of abject horror. You've given me that look every time we meet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But uh, where is he?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Paimon can't see him! So is he... a spirit? A ghost? Wait...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is it because I made physical contact with Haypasia? Is The Balladeer in her consciousness?)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I can hear all of your thoughts, you know.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Don't you remember? I already "saw" you the first time you came to Pardis Dhyai and made contact with Haypasia.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What did you do to Haypasia?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I didn't need to do anything. It is her honor to be able to connect her consciousness with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, who are you talking to? ...It can't be The Balladeer, right? Hehe, that's impossible...

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I know you must be curious. I might as well tell you that I decided to enter Haypasia's consciousness the moment I sensed your touch.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But why?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I wanted to observe you on a fool's errand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}! Wh—What are you doing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, please stay quiet for now...

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: My deification is nearly complete. All that's left now are just some final details.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Do you understand? Even if you manage to rescue Lesser Lord Kusanali, it will be impossible for you to defeat a bona fide god like me.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Is it wise to force that childlike god into a divine battle against me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Akademiya acted even faster than we thought...)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Scholars consider the God of Wisdom to be the sum total of their faith. It's how they can justify reverence for a god as they construct it.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: But this also shows that humanity's worship of gods is a combination of blasphemy and exaltation. It's truly laughable.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If you can hear my thoughts, I want to ask you a question.)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Yes, what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (You're acting more friendly than usual, or am I mistaken?)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'm in a good mood, which is why I'm talking to you like this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...But, are you really okay with all this?)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Akademiya plans to infuse your consciousness with Divine Knowledge Capsules... this is extremely risky.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Even if the Akademiya's theories are correct, and you manage to gain the wisdom of a god...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (You would probably no longer remain yourself. You will become the new "Greater Lord Rukkhadevata" for the Akademiya.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Even if it means losing yourself, would you still want to become a god?)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Hmph, those words almost make you sound like a friend who actually cares.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: But you're wrong. I'm different from all of you.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I was born to become a god. My entire life up until this point has just been a meaningless routine.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Just think about a sheet of paper... By itself, it holds no meaning. The content recorded on it is what gives it value.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: All "I" had recorded down before were some painful memories and boring human feelings. Such senseless drivel should have been erased a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Indeed, to me, the sight of you fools and your futile struggles is far more amusing. Tell me, just what has this world done for you to protect it with such zest and conviction?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...You wouldn't understand.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: I'm connected to your consciousness, so I can hear what you're thinking and sense the depth of your determination.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: This is a good conversation we're having, so here's a word of advice... Let go of your misguided guardian complex. You know nothing about the truth.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: It'll be for your own good, as well as everyone else's. Humans are a species that can only find bliss in ignorance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...If that's truly what you believe, why did you keep your connection with Haypasia? Surely, with the power you've come to possess, you can cut her off with just a thought.)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Ah, you've seen my affection for her. If you were in my position, I think you'd feel the same way.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: She peered into my consciousness and saw my past. Someone like that is qualified to become my first follower.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: All gods need followers, so Haypasia has been chosen. Her appearance heralds my imminent arrival at the throne of divinity, while her worship shall become my glory.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Is that so?)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: You're doubting me again? No matter. Soon, you'll know what kind of authority you're challenging.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If you truly cherish your follower, you should protect her from harm.)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Who wants to hurt my devout follower?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It seems that The Doctor does not wish for her to stay in Sumeru and continue receiving treatment here. Isn't that a little suspicious?)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: The Doctor wants to hurt my first follower?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Doesn't that make you mad?)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Hehehe...

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: ...Hahahaha. How very amusing. Has anyone ever told you that you're not good at sowing discord?

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: The Doctor has never known his place. Even now, the puny human thinks himself capable of interfering in the business of the new god.

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: You're still too naive if you think a few words will be enough to convince me to destroy The Doctor, but I'm willing to give you a gift, just like my expression of affection towards Haypasia...

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: It is an honor for you to be able to stand here and speak with me. As my listener, you will be rewarded.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That look on your face... What are you planning?)

dialogues.speaker: The Balladeer
dialogues.text: Both good things and bad things can be called gifts. After all, gods have never needed to be reasonable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaah!? Paimon hears thunder!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thunder!? Could it be The Balladeer?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That person Paimon couldn't see was The Balladeer? He sure chatted with you for a while!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh? Where is the storm headed!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It can't be... Is The Balladeer using the Gnosis to change the weather?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means anyone outside is in danger! Let's go, Tighnari and Dehya still must be fighting!

choices.text: He's become... milder, but somehow, even more deranged.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, have the Fatui retreated?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tighnari and Dehya are over there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What happened to you!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: He's hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm fine... Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't move. I've seen Eremites get struck by lightning before. You need to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Struck by lightning!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We were fighting, and just as things started looking grim, the weather suddenly became extremely strange. Lightning started attacking everyone, almost as if it were alive.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Luckily, there were only two of us, and both of us were nimble enough to dodge most of the strikes. There were a lot of Fatui, though, and they were being torn to shreds by the bolts of lightning.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: With that, all the Fatui soldiers were forced to retreat...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: It's alright.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: My wound aside, you look like... you've seen something unpleasant. Is Haypasia alright?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She's okay for now, but I want to tell you something.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Ugh...!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hey! Didn't I tell you not to move?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Just in case... Ugh! Let's... go to Haypasia's place, and talk about things there.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Why are you sorry?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I might have triggered the thunder and lightning...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Huh... It's alright, I'm sure you also never expected this to happen. Don't blame yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Thank goodness, she's fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, how about taking care of yourself first?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I understand my condition... *grimace* The wound is not fatal. I'll be alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, the more you understand medicine, the worse of a patient you become...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I know. They always think they can push through the pain.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ugh... agh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, he sat down!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #Let me rest for a bit... *exhale* Sorry, {NICKNAME}, now you may start.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You recount everything from "meeting" The Doctor at Port Ormos to your encounter with The Balladeer while checking up on Haypasia.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what you were talking to The Balladeer about? Paimon can't believe what he's thinking...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Akademiya's... god creation plan... How ridiculous.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That sounds, uh... ambitious, I guess? Anyway, this is all way beyond me.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: As long as I can enjoy every day with a drink in my hand, tasty food in my stomach, and a good night's rest, that's enough. I'll only work when I have to.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ahaha, I must be the least ambitious person who's ever set foot in Pardis Dhyai.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Don't say that. I haven't even thanked you for your help back there.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Well, if nothing else, all this proves that The Doctor really did have some urgent matter to attend to, and left Sumeru in a hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, and I also have a theory.

choices.text: I think The Balladeer is the reason why The Doctor is targeting Haypasia.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hmm. Maybe the Fatui want to cover up some secret of The Balladeer? Is that why they tried to seize Haypasia?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You said The Balladeer claimed that Haypasia has seen his past... So what could be there?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: For now, I'm still not really sure.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Have you noticed? The Balladeer is not happy with The Doctor's actions. He thinks The Doctor has no right to consider himself as his equal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, if The Doctor was to show up again, would The Balladeer zap him with lightning?

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: #Based on what {NICKNAME} has said, I think he would. Having The Doctor gone benefits him as well as us.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: In other words, we've successfully completed this stage of the plan! The Doctor is out of the picture now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay, that's a big accomplishment!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Ugh! I'm... also happy for you.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Thank you for the help, Tighnari. Make sure you rest up for now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, please do get some rest.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Yeah, yeah... alright.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: #Okay, that wraps things up for us here at Pardis Dhyai. {NICKNAME}, it's about time we rendezvous with the others at the Grand Bazaar.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Let's continue to keep a low profile. You can head there once you're ready.

choices.text: Her consciousness connected to The Balladeer, and she has seen his past...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Alright, everyone is here.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: How did everything go? Any luck with your missions?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's each report back one by one. I'll start first.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We have made the necessary modifications to the Akasha Terminal. In addition, the props required are also ready.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #I'll go next. {NICKNAME} and I went to Pardis Dhyai. The situation was a bit complicated, but we found Tighnari. Unfortunately, he was wounded during a fight.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Who was behind it?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #Uh... Well, that's the tough part... What should I say, {NICKNAME}? "The Fatui" or "The Balladeer"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go with "The Balladeer."

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: After some back-and-forth, we confirmed that The Doctor has left Sumeru by boat. He has something urgent to attend to back in Snezhnaya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So, we've successfully removed The Doctor from the picture. Also, Tighnari's already resting, so he'll be okay.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Tighnari also asked us to tell you this message! "Trust your own senses and experiences."

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alright... I'll remember that.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Everything also went smoothly on my side. The Eremites should have arrived at their destination by now.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: To avoid alerting the quarry, they will stay there for now.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I can't believe you actually got so many Eremites into Sumeru City!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to Rahman and his brave team, as well as their bold strategy.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It appears to have been very effective. I'm glad to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, is that everything? Okay, this meeting is adjourned.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, you mean that's it?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, what else is there to discuss?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Shouldn't you end with some words of encouragement? You know, to fire us up now?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Personally, I'd rather we all go home and get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Alhaitham, you... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Oh, and if you wanted someone to say something to that effect, then I must reiterate that I'm here to strategize, not to lead.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So you should find someone more suitable to do that.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But I thought all of you Akademiya big-shots were great speakers?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Then I should remind you that I'm the Scribe.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I know that, so what?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: A Scribe is responsible for recording meetings, not speaking.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Fine, whatever.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Well, Cyno doesn't seem to be much of a talker, either. I guess that leaves it to my "employer."

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Employer?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #Yep, {NICKNAME} hired me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She asked for a smile as her payment.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haha, that's right. So c'mon, boss! What do you have to say for the team?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Say something to boost morale!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm... let me think...
Huh? What are you all doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Nilou!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Hey everyone! I'm not disturbing you, am I?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Not at all. I was actually just about to go find you.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Heehee. Uh, judging from the group and all your serious faces, you were discussing something important, weren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: But you also look like you're up to no good... Haha, seems pretty interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Welcome, Nilou. Would you like to join us?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Huh? Join you?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: You mean... you also want to discuss something important... with me?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes, something very important.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Nilou, are there any breaks in your performance schedule in the upcoming days?

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, you're seriously inviting me?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Alhaitham tells Nilou of the plan on Jnagarbha Day...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nilou is shocked at first, but it isn't long before she's bubbling with excitement and anticipation.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I... I can't believe my ears! You are truly the bravest and most passionate people of Sumeru, well, that... I've ever met!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: #Oh right, {NICKNAME} and Paimon are not from Sumeru, but you are awesome as well!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's right!

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: I... I must admit that I'm a little scared.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: But I'll try my best for Lesser Lord Kusanali. If I can somehow use my abilities to help you, then count me in.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Remember, believe in yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: ...Okay! I'll get my friends at the Grand Bazaar to help us tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Just remember not to say too much. Be discreet.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Yep, you got it!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: All the preparations are done. Now, can we finally conclude this meeting?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah. Tomorrow, we are going to save a god.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: So, have you thought up what you'd like to say, boss?

choices.text: It's hard to believe everything that has happened till now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep yep! It's a grand plan, and we're all super awesome!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's right, so...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just get a good night's sleep, everyone!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hahaha!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Well said. A good night's rest before an operation can be the difference between success and failure.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: ...Thankfully, I've had my place to myself recently. It's been nice and quiet.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Oh, huh, nothing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, let's all go home and get a good night's sleep, so we can be up early tomorrow!

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Okay, so I guess that means it's time to say goodnight now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! Goodnight, everyone.

choices.text: And our actions will bring change to many things tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's over there! Let's go say hi.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Heh, that Harbinger may have tried to cover his trail, but he still left some traces.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Or perhaps, he never even thought about concealing his whereabouts. Maybe that's just how arrogant he really is...

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: Now, THIS is a proper farewell ceremony for a Snezhnayan Harbinger!

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Soldier
dialogues.text: The Lord Harbinger is leaving... *sigh* I've still only seen him once or twice...

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: No, no, I remember it like it was yesterday! Both his expressions and tones are now very different.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Sergeant
dialogues.text: Also, for some reason, he seems like he's... all smiles now.

dialogues.speaker: Fatui Soldier
dialogues.text: You must be mistaken... Nobody's supposed to look happy when they're on a business trip.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Yep, we're headed in the right direction.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The traces are still fresh, but there's no sign of his entourage. Clearly, they're in a hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The Doctor is on that boat.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmph, so he told the truth after all. He is actually leaving Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Let's get closer and find a place to hide so we can observe him.
